name: playbook
title: Playbook
description: A phone-first handbook with a complete contents page, numbered how-tos, troubleshooting sections and clear printed sheets. Choosing this look does not restrict who can read a site.

content.purpose: The handbook name in the top bar.
One sentence explaining how to use the handbook.
One stream per part, with a title and intro. Sections sets the part order; every entry is listed, newest first within each part.
The pinned help link, for example If something is down; set cta_link to the breaks tag page of the troubleshooting stream. Tags are per stream.
Set home to Contents for the sticky link back to the current part on the contents page.

Use You need, Steps, Done when, If it fails for how-tos; You will see, Check first, Fix, Who to ask, Do not for troubleshooting; Why for guides; Related for links. Use ordered lists for steps. Headings get stable anchors. A final Last verified by paragraph remains ordinary text. Reference material can use lists or a monospaced code block; Markdown tables are not supported.
Use guide, how-to, breaks or reference as a small type label. Keep troubleshooting entries together in one stream so its breaks tag page lists every symptom.

art.ask: Ask whether a diagram or screenshot is needed to explain a step. A text-only handbook needs no pictures.
art.style: Clear instructional screenshots or diagrams supplied by the owner; no decorative images.
art.prompt_prefix: A simple instructional diagram with only the necessary labels.
steps: Start with text, grouped into parts and short pages.
Use neutral sample content to check the look before adding real material.
If a picture is needed, confirm its accuracy and write useful alt text.
Check the contents link, numbered steps, troubleshooting sections and print layout on a phone and desktop.
